newsitem.title: USA: Nicotine could eventually be banned under agreement.
newsitem.headline: Nicotine could eventually be banned under agreement.

text.p: A landmark agreement with the tobacco industry would formally recognise that the Food and Drug Administration has regulatory power over tobacco products and could eventually ban nicotine, state attorneys general announced on Friday.
Companies violating the regulations would face large penalties under an historic agreement between U.S. states and the tobacco industry, a statement said.

The agreement would recognise that the FDA has regulatory power over tobacco products, including the authority to reduce the levels of nicotine and eventually eliminate it "if appropriate," the statement said.
The agreement would enact into law current FDA rules to protect children from tobacco marketing.

It also would require FDA approval of all ingredients in tobacco products and standards for reducing harmful components including nicotine. The proposed agreement mandates testing of ingredients and safety assessments, the statement said.

The agreement would require the tobacco industry to hand over to the FDA all research it conducts. It would also impose penalties for any violations that are ten times those facing other companies regulated by the FDA, the attorneys general said.
